title: They didn’t just lose a battle.
paragraphs: They didn’t just lose a battle.
They were erased.
Men. Women. Children. Entire nations wiped out—and it was God who commanded it.
That tension should shake you.
Because this is the same God who says, “Love your enemies.”
So what’s going on?
Here’s what we miss…

God wasn’t acting out of rage.
He was executing judgment after centuries of mercy.

In Genesis 15:16, God tells Abraham something chilling:
The sin of the Canaanites “has not yet reached its full measure.”
Translation?
Judgment was delayed.
For hundreds of years.

These nations weren’t innocent villages.
They practiced brutal evil—child sacrifice, ritual violence, corruption that poisoned everything.
By the time you reach Deuteronomy and Joshua, this wasn’t sudden.
It was final.
But here’s where grace walks in.
Even in judgment… God made a way out.
A prostitute named Rahab—living in that doomed city—chose to believe.
And God spared her.
Not just spared.
He redeemed her story and placed her in the lineage of Jesus (see Matthew 1).
Let that sink in.
In the middle of destruction, mercy was still available.
So what does this mean for us?
God is not cruel.
He is holy.
And holiness confronts evil—fully, finally, justly.
But He is also patient.
And right now, you’re living in that patience.
Because the same God who judged nations…
Sent His Son to be judged for you.
At the cross, wrath and mercy collided.
Jesus took the destruction we deserved.
This isn’t just history.
It’s a warning.
And an invitation.

Judgment is real.
But so is grace.
Turn while there’s still time.
Run to Christ—not away from Him.

Because from scandal to grace—
Jesus rewrites everything.
